title: Pennsylvania Reports Fifth Measles Death as Outbreak Continues
subtitle: State health officials and federal agencies disagree on death counts while the virus spreads to 39 counties.

summary.en: Pennsylvania has confirmed its fifth death linked to an ongoing measles outbreak. The state has now recorded nearly 1,000 cases across 39 counties. Most people who caught the virus were not vaccinated. A disagreement has emerged between state and federal officials regarding how to count these deaths. Health experts warn that the virus is highly contagious and can have serious long-term health effects.
summary.zh: 賓夕法尼亞州確認了第五起與持續中的麻疹疫情相關的死亡病例。該州目前在 39 個郡累計記錄了近 1,000 例確診。大多數感染病毒的患者皆未接種疫苗。州政府與聯邦官員之間對於如何統計這些死亡病例出現了分歧。衛生專家警告，該病毒傳染力極強，且可能造成嚴重的長期健康影響。

paragraphs.en: Pennsylvania health officials announced on Wednesday that a fifth person has died from measles in the state. This latest death occurred in Lancaster County, an area that has been at the center of a large outbreak since it began in late April. According to The Guardian Health, the individual was not vaccinated. Due to privacy rules, the state has not shared more details about the person who died.
paragraphs.zh: 賓夕法尼亞州衛生官員週三宣布，該州出現第五起麻疹死亡病例。這起最新死亡案例發生在蘭開斯特郡，該地區自四月下旬以來一直是疫情爆發的核心地帶。根據衛報健康版（The Guardian Health）報導，該名死者生前未接種疫苗。基於隱私規範，州政府並未公開關於死者的更多細節。

paragraphs.en: This new death brings the total number of confirmed cases in Pennsylvania to 943 across 39 counties. The Pennsylvania Department of Health reports that 176 people have been hospitalized during this period. The Guardian Health noted that less than 1% of these cases involved people who had received the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. This vaccine is known to be 97% effective at preventing the disease.
paragraphs.zh: 這起新增死亡病例使賓夕法尼亞州 39 個郡的累計確診總數達到 943 例。賓夕法尼亞州衛生廳指出，在此期間已有 176 人住院治療。衛報健康版提到，這些病例中僅不到百分之一的患者曾接種過麻疹、腮腺炎及德國麻疹（MMR）混合疫苗。已知該疫苗在預防此疾病方面的有效率高達百分之九十七。

paragraphs.en: A significant disagreement has developed between Pennsylvania officials and the federal Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). While Pennsylvania counts five deaths related to the virus, the CDC has not included these in its national total. According to The Guardian Health, this is because the current federal government changed its method for reporting such deaths. Furthermore, US health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has publicly questioned whether the deaths in Pennsylvania were caused by the measles virus or other health conditions. In response, Pennsylvania officials have warned that they might stop asking for federal emergency help if the CDC does not recognize the deaths reported by the state.
paragraphs.zh: 賓夕法尼亞州官員與聯邦疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）之間出現了嚴重分歧。儘管賓州統計了五起與該病毒相關的死亡病例，但聯邦疾病管制與預防中心並未將其納入全國總數。根據衛報健康版報導，這是因為現任聯邦政府改變了此類死亡病例的通報方式。此外，美國衛生部長小羅伯特·甘迺迪（Robert F. Kennedy Jr.）公開質疑賓州的死亡病例究竟是由麻疹病毒引起，還是由其他健康狀況所致。對此，賓州官員警告，若聯邦疾病管制與預防中心不承認該州通報的死亡病例，他們可能會停止請求聯邦緊急援助。

paragraphs.en: Measles is considered one of the most contagious diseases known to medicine. It spreads through the air when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or even just breathes. According to NPR Health, people do not need to touch an infected person to catch the virus; simply being in the same room within two hours of someone who has it can be enough to become infected. Dr. Paul Offit, an expert at the Children’s Hospital of Philadelphia, explained that one person with measles can infect up to 18 other people if those individuals have not been vaccinated or have never had the disease before.
paragraphs.zh: 麻疹被認為是醫學界已知最具傳染性的疾病之一。當感染者咳嗽、打噴嚏甚至僅是呼吸時，病毒就會透過空氣傳播。根據美國公共廣播電台健康版（NPR Health）報導，人們不需要接觸感染者也可能染病；只要與患者在同一空間待過，即便是在對方離開後的兩小時內，都有可能受到感染。費城兒童醫院的專家保羅·奧菲特（Paul Offit）醫師解釋，若接觸者未曾接種疫苗或未曾感染過此病，一名麻疹患者最多可傳染給 18 個人。

paragraphs.en: Health experts are concerned that the true number of cases may be higher than what is officially recorded. Dr. Offit noted that many people might not visit a doctor when they get sick, meaning they are not counted in the official data. Dr. Kalyani McCullough from the California Department of Public Health warned that measles is not just a simple fever with a rash. She explained that it can cause long-term damage to the body, including a condition called "immune amnesia," where the virus makes it harder for the body to fight off other infections in the future.
paragraphs.zh: 衛生專家擔心，實際病例數可能高於官方紀錄。奧菲特醫師指出，許多人在生病時可能不會就醫，因此未被計入官方數據中。加州公共衛生廳的卡莉亞妮·麥卡洛（Kalyani McCullough）醫師警告，麻疹並非僅是伴隨紅疹的普通發燒。她解釋，麻疹會對身體造成長期損害，包括一種稱為「免疫失憶」的症狀，即病毒會導致人體未來更難以抵抗其他感染。

paragraphs.en: As the outbreak continues, the state is working to increase vaccination rates. According to The Guardian Health, staff at state health centers have already given more than 5,500 MMR vaccines through 180 temporary clinics. More clinics are planned for the coming weeks. However, experts are worried about a general decline in vaccination rates among young children, which they suggest is linked to confusion and misinformation about vaccines.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著疫情持續，該州正致力於提高疫苗接種率。根據衛報健康版報導，州衛生中心的醫護人員已透過 180 個臨時診所施打了超過 5,500 劑 MMR 疫苗。未來幾週還計畫增設更多診所。然而，專家們對於幼童疫苗接種率普遍下降感到擔憂，並認為這與針對疫苗的混亂資訊及錯誤訊息有關。

paragraphs.en: Across the United States, there have been more than 3,600 reported cases of measles in 2026. While the country was declared free of the disease in 2000, recent outbreaks in states like Ohio, New York, and Pennsylvania have made it difficult to keep that status. Ars Technica reported that before these recent deaths, Pennsylvania had not seen a measles-related death in 35 years. The other victims in the current Pennsylvania outbreak included two infants who were too young to be vaccinated, an 18-year-old with a severe brain complication, and a 40-year-old woman with other health issues.
paragraphs.zh: 2026 年全美通報的麻疹病例已超過 3,600 例。雖然美國曾在 2000 年宣布消除該疾病，但近期在俄亥俄州、紐約州和賓夕法尼亞州爆發的疫情，使得維持該狀態變得困難。科技媒體 Ars Technica 報導稱，在這些近期死亡病例發生前，賓夕法尼亞州已有 35 年未出現麻疹相關死亡案例。賓州此次疫情的其他受害者包括兩名年紀太小而無法接種疫苗的嬰兒、一名患有嚴重腦部併發症的 18 歲青少年，以及一名患有其他健康問題的 40 歲女性。

paragraphs.en: For now, health officials continue to monitor the situation closely. They emphasize that the MMR vaccine remains the best way to protect against the virus. Residents are encouraged to check their vaccination status and stay informed as the state works to control the spread of the disease in affected communities.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，衛生官員持續密切監控疫情。他們強調，MMR 疫苗仍是預防該病毒的最佳方式。當局鼓勵居民檢查自己的疫苗接種狀態，並在州政府努力控制疫情擴散的同時，隨時關注相關資訊。

previousArticles.title: Pennsylvania Faces Growing Measles Crisis as Deaths Rise
previousArticles.summaryEn: Pennsylvania has recorded its fifth measles-related death as the state struggles with a major outbreak. Over 900 cases have been confirmed across 39 counties, mostly among unvaccinated individuals. The state government is currently in a dispute with federal health agencies regarding how to count these deaths. Experts warn that measles is highly contagious and can cause serious long-term health problems. Public health officials continue to organize vaccination clinics to stop the spread of the virus.

quiz.question: According to the article, what is notable about the individuals who have died from measles in Pennsylvania during the current outbreak?

options.A: All of the victims were children under the age of five.
options.B: The victims included individuals with pre-existing health complications or age-related vulnerabilities.
options.C: Every person who died had previously received the MMR vaccine.
options.D: All five victims were residents of the same household in Lancaster County.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第七段，死者包括兩名年紀太小無法接種疫苗的嬰兒、一名有嚴重腦部併發症的 18 歲青年，以及一名有其他健康問題的 40 歲女性，顯示死者皆有年齡或健康上的脆弱性。選項 A 錯誤，因為死者年齡層不限於五歲以下；選項 C 錯誤，因為文章第二段提到不到 1% 的病例是已接種者，且死者多為未接種；選項 D 錯誤，文章僅提到疫情中心在 Lancaster County，並未說明死者來自同一家庭。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between the Pennsylvania Department of Health and the federal CDC regarding the current measles outbreak?

options.A: They are working together to create a new, unified reporting system for measles deaths.
options.B: The CDC has officially apologized to Pennsylvania for ignoring their data.
options.C: There is a significant disagreement regarding the classification of deaths, leading to potential friction in government cooperation.
options.D: The CDC is providing extra funding to Pennsylvania because they recognize the severity of the outbreak.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三段，賓州官員與 CDC 對於死亡人數的計算存在分歧，CDC 未將賓州的死亡案例納入國家總數，這導致賓州官員威脅若 CDC 不承認其數據，將停止要求聯邦緊急援助。選項 A 錯誤，文中未提及雙方合作建立新系統；選項 B 錯誤，文中並未提到 CDC 有任何道歉行為；選項 D 錯誤，文中提到的是賓州可能停止要求聯邦援助，而非獲得額外資金。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the term 'immune amnesia' suggest about the effect of the measles virus on the human body?

options.A: It causes the body to forget how to identify and fight off various types of future infections.
options.B: It creates a temporary memory loss that affects the patient's ability to recognize people.
options.C: It makes the immune system overreact and attack the body's own healthy tissues.
options.D: It forces the body to produce too many white blood cells, leading to extreme exhaustion.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。根據文章第五段，Dr. Kalyani McCullough 解釋「免疫失憶症」（immune amnesia）是指病毒使身體在未來更難對抗其他感染。這是一種比喻用法，意指免疫系統「忘記」了如何防禦。選項 B 錯誤，這是對「amnesia」一詞的字面誤解，與記憶力喪失無關；選項 C 錯誤，文中未提到免疫系統攻擊自身組織；選項 D 錯誤，文中並未描述白血球產量過剩的問題。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding the measles outbreak in Pennsylvania?

options.A: The MMR vaccine is no longer effective against new strains of the measles virus.
options.B: The federal government is solely responsible for the rapid spread of measles in the United States.
options.C: Measles is a highly contagious disease, and despite the effectiveness of vaccines, the current outbreak highlights serious public health and reporting challenges.
options.D: Most people who catch measles will require hospitalization, regardless of their vaccination status.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。本文綜合報導了賓州的麻疹疫情、疫苗的有效性、官方數據統計的爭議，以及專家對於疫情擴散與公共衛生影響的擔憂，涵蓋了文章的核心內容。選項 A 錯誤，文章強調疫苗仍有 97% 的保護力；選項 B 錯誤，文章並未指責聯邦政府是疫情擴散的主因；選項 D 錯誤，文章提到 943 例中僅 176 人住院，並非大多數人皆需住院。
